title: BFS pathfinding
summary: Shortest paths on a grid: how enemies find the player.

cards.title: Rings of equal distance
cards.body:
Breadth-first search explores everything 1 step away, then 2, then 3. The first time it reaches the goal, it has found a **shortest** path, because every shorter distance was explored first.

It's the same BFS as cluster pays in the Slot Lab, plus a `parent` table to rebuild the route.
Edit the maze in the Algorithm Lab: `.` floor, `#` wall, rows separated by `/`.

cards.question: Why is the first time BFS reaches the goal guaranteed to be a shortest path?
choices: Because it goes towards the goal
Because cells are explored in order of distance
cards.explain: The queue processes all distance-d cells before any distance-(d+1) cell. If a shorter route existed, it would have reached the goal earlier. (This needs equal step costs; otherwise use Dijkstra.)
